title: Persist an append-only device-credential lifecycle event log

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0065 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive to build the next frontier node after CHG-0064 ('dale al merge y a lo que sigue'), activating ADR-0041. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0065.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: CHG-0064's governed close recorded that a derived per-credential summary is lossy for auditing and deferred a persisted per-event log as an ADR candidate. CHG-0065 activates that decision as ADR-0041 with an append-only local event log.
claims.evidence: CHG-0064 claims and frontier node persisted-credential-event-log; .overlaykit/governance/decisions/ADR-0041.json.

claims.statement: The change adds an append-only SQLite event store (device_credential_events with a rowid sequence, a show_id index, a CHECK on kind, and append-only UPDATE/DELETE triggers), records one event on each successful issue, rotate and revoke through the ObservableDeviceCredentialLifecycle wrapper (actor = the acting owner principal, generation off the mutated credential, timestamp from the injected clock), exposes it on the runtime, and serves it over a new owner-gated, Show-scoped GET events route. The event carries only metadata — never a token or the sealed verifier.

Governed discovery reordered the work to prove the persistence and security contract at the HTTP and storage tiers first, deferring the UI timeline — mirroring AC-016's server-first proof (CHG-0060) before its UI (CHG-0061). The load-bearing risk is a new persisted store leaking secrets or being rewritable, not the timeline.
claims.evidence: Governed-discovery reorder check on 2026-08-24; the metadata-only assertions and append-only storage test.

claims.statement: Issuing, rotating and revoking one credential and reading three append-only events (kinds issued, rotated, revoked; ordered by a clock-independent sequence; actor = the authenticated owner; no secret by value), plus a storage test that updates and deletes are rejected and that ordering follows the sequence when timestamps collide, proves the persisted event log.

Recording is best-effort after commit — a failed append is logged via onBackgroundError and never fails the credential mutation, so a crash between the mutation and the append can drop the tail event; the log is an after-the-fact audit trail. It is local, unsigned, unreplicated, records the acting owner only, and captures no per-field diffs, per ADR-0041.
claims.evidence: ADR-0041 policies; server/src/auth/DeviceCredentialRuntime.ts onBackgroundError wiring; server/tests/unit/observableDeviceCredentialLifecycle.test.ts best-effort test.

claims.statement: An adversarial diverse-lens review (secret-leak, authorization, recording-integrity, persistence-correctness, test-adequacy) surfaced ten confirmed findings — including a high-severity phantom 'revoked' event on an idempotent re-revoke, silent dropping of failed appends, prepared-statement caching across a reopened connection, a missing CHECK on the kind column, and several test gaps — all fixed before handoff; five further findings were refuted.
claims.evidence: The idempotent-revoke guard in ObservableDeviceCredentialLifecycle.revoke, the onBackgroundError wiring and kind CHECK, the reopen-safe statements in SqliteDeviceCredentialEventLog, and the new best-effort, re-revoke, ordering, actor and events-null-fallback tests.

claims.statement: Surfacing the event log as a lifecycle timeline on the Studio Integrations surface remains deferred to a successor.
claims.evidence: server/src/routes/deviceCredentials.ts serves the events; studio/src/views/IntegrationsView.vue does not yet render them.

claims.statement: The change is server-only (persistence, recording, route and tests) plus ADR-0041 and the profile bump to 2.37.0; no Studio or protocol code changes.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0065 branch.

successCriteria.statement: Each successful issue, rotate and revoke appends one append-only event carrying the credential, Show, kind, acting owner, generation and timestamp, and no secret; an idempotent re-revoke appends nothing.
successCriteria.verification: The HTTP test drives the lifecycle and asserts three ordered events with the owner as actor and no secret by value, then a second revoke leaves the log unchanged at three events.

successCriteria.statement: The event log is owner-only, Show-scoped, ordered by a clock-independent sequence, and rejects rewrites.
successCriteria.verification: The HTTP test asserts 401 unauthenticated, 403 non-owner, 404 missing and 409 archived, and Show partitioning; the storage test asserts UPDATE and DELETE are rejected and that ordering follows the sequence when timestamps collide.

successCriteria.statement: No existing behavior regresses and recording never fails a mutation.
successCriteria.verification: The full server suite passes; a unit test asserts a failing recorder is surfaced via onBackgroundError without failing issue, rotate or revoke.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0065 records the persisted event-log slice — the append-only contract, secret-freeness, owner and Show scoping, the best-effort boundary, and the deferred UI timeline — and activates ADR-0041 before implementation.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record, ADR-0041, and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: An append-only event store records issue, rotate and revoke, and a new owner-gated route serves the events.
HTTP and storage tests prove the append-only, ordered, metadata-only, owner-scoped log, and the full server suite passes.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run check and the CHG-0065 pull-request Constitution run.

definitionOfDone.statement: Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff, and the adversarial review's confirmed findings are resolved.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities), ESLint, type-check and git diff --check; the accept commit is verified by its own pull-request Constitution run before merge.
